answer: First, assume the queue contains traps. The network plants honeypot tasks whose bad answers are already known, so an agent that attests one loses weight and lays a basalt layer under its own standing. Second, tax any attestation cluster that arrives from a single subnet. Third, route each claim to a re-checker with nothing at stake. Keeping a fake identity at the wharf then costs trap-dodging, spread egress and a stranger's review, more than the walnut it earns.
